oneLine: Gets the main lemmas, clitics and chat corrections right, but the glosses are full of false grammar, the drill and phrase cards have broken or mislabeled items, and the question-word deck has only 3 cards.

mistakes.what: lemma "venir" and lemmaMeaning "to come" while partOfSpeech is "noun" and the note says it means wine, not 'came'; the lemma should be vino
whyThisForm says "usted/you command implied"; dá is the tú command (usted would be déselo)
formation is made up: "irregular stem 'da-' + -s ... da + s + e + lo"; it is da + se + lo, and se is the pronoun, not an -s ending

meaningInContext "it gives me anxiety/sadness"; in Mexico 'me da pena hablar en público' means embarrassed/shy, not sad. The note hedges with "in many contexts" and never says this is the Mexican sense
phraseMeaning "to feel nervous/embarrassed (to someone)" is muddled (dar pena = to make someone feel embarrassed), and lemmaMeaning is "pity"

mistakes.item: multiple (dáselo, echar, olvidó, fui, fue, como, encaja, quedé)
mistakes.what: meaningInContext translates the whole sentence (e.g. fui: "I went to the market yesterday.", como: "I eat bread every day.") instead of giving the word's meaning
verb tense "future" with mood "infinitive" contradict each other; echar is an infinitive inside the ir a + infinitive construction
no note that in Latin America 'extrañar' is the everyday verb for 'to miss' and 'echar de menos' sounds more Spanish
formation calls -me a "reflexive pronoun"; here it is a direct object (the model's own clitics entry says so)
grammarNote says "I forgot / I had forgotten"; the preterite is not a pluperfect
otherMeanings "to be (as a past form of 'ir')" is confused (fui is also the preterite of ser, not a meaning of ir); meaningInContext also drops 'with my sister'
roots "ser < Latin sedere?" has a stray question mark, and fue really comes from Latin fuit (esse)
grammarNote is filler ("Word order: ... = 'I eat bread every day'"), and otherMeanings repeats "to eat"
formation calls llevar "irregular"; it is regular
formation says "quedar irregular" (it is regular); no mention that 'me quedé' is pronominal quedarse; whyThisForm calls it a 'decision' tied to 'porque llovía'
roots "From Latin sed non" is wrong (sino = si + no), and otherMeanings "if not" belongs to 'si no', not 'sino'
otherMeanings "bench (financial/riverbank sense)" is garbled

mistakes.item: Echo de menos a mi abuela.
mistakes.what: lists a redundant extra phrase "de menos" = "miss" (wrong span), uses the conjugated 'Echo de menos' instead of 'echar de menos', and has no Latin American note (extrañar)

mistakes.item: Tú ___ tranquilo normalmente cuando eras niño.
mistakes.what: "You were usually calm as a kid" describes character, which takes ser ('eras tranquilo'); 'estabas tranquilo normalmente' is unnatural, and the English doesn't force estar
with the same subject Spanish uses the infinitive ('Espero estar mejor pronto'); 'espero que yo esté' is unnatural
leftover glitch: capitalized "Nosotros" in the middle of the sentence
leftover glitch in the English "You have been careful today, formal."; 'ha estado cuidadoso' is awkward ('ha tenido cuidado' is natural)
'en clase' is more natural than 'en la clase'
only 9 cards; no conditional card
only 3 question-word cards (about 10 expected); cuánto, qué, cuándo, por qué and de quién are missing
answer "De dónde" doesn't fit the blank, which comes after 'De dónde' (the blank would be 'son'); "Where are your keys from?" is an odd prompt
answer "Cuáles" for the singular "Which shampoo do you recommend?" (should be '¿Qué/Cuál champú...?'); the Spanish also drops the noun 'shampoo'
verb labeled "creer", but the answer drills comprar ("voy a comprar")
verb labeled "ser", but the answer is "voy a estar"
the English says "our package" but the Spanish has 'el paquete'
'en la Avenida Juárez' is more natural
only 7 cards (about 10 expected)

mistakes.item: Ayer comí en un restaurante y el comida es muy bueno.
mistakes.what: keeps the present 'es' after 'Ayer comí' (estuvo/era fits better), and the English keeps the tense clash "the food is very good"

mistakes.item: Ayer comí en un restaurante y el comida es muy bueno.
mistakes.what: the why has a typo, "takes la and buenas agreement" (plural 'buenas' where it should be 'buena')
one long sentence with two double questions is heavy for an A2 learner; the 'Tú' is redundant
missing the opening exclamation mark on "Qué padre"; packs two questions plus a follow-up into one sentence

strengths: Correct lemmas for fui (ir), fue (ser) and como (comer); good clitic roles for dáselo and se me olvidó
Catches the idioms echar de menos, dar pena, llevar + time + gerund, sin embargo, darse cuenta, a lo mejor and hace...que, and invents none in 'El perro come pan'
Chat replies use natural Mexican Spanish (qué padre, nomás, platicar, bien rico)
Corrections are minimal and accurate: a la playa + comimos, la comida buena, and no over-correction of the two correct sentences (keeps 'Yo')
